hints: The route must use exactly k flights, and a cheapest route may revisit cities.
Store the minimum direct edge cost from i to j, or infinity if none exists.
Use matrix multiplication where combining paths adds costs and choosing between them takes the minimum.
analogy: The min-plus version of matrix multiplication combines route costs instead of counting routes.
example: If i->j costs 4 and j->k costs 3, that two-flight route costs 7.
algorithm: Set matrix A[i][j] to the cheapest direct edge. Binary exponentiate under min-plus operations: product[i][j]=min over x of left[i][x]+right[x][j]. Answer A^k[1][n], or -1 if unreachable.
correctness: Each matrix power represents the cheapest walk of that exact length; the min over intermediate city x considers every possible split of the route.
complexity: O(n^3 log k) time and O(n^2) space.
